svg.title: How the research assistant works
svg.desc: Animated diagram. A question is searched in 21 fictional documents, a model reads one figure per document, fixed rules judge the evidence, a router answers, searches again with a rewritten query, or sends the run to a person. Checkpoints save the state so a run can pause and resume.
svg.text: A question goes in, an evidence-based answer comes out. Every box says who does the work.

g.text: Question 1: what is the average annual fee
Round 1: the search compares the question with all 21 documents
and keeps the relevant ones: E1, E2 and E3.
Two collectors work in parallel and merge their documents
into the shared state, without duplicates.
The model reads one figure per document:
The rules judge: the copy counts once and weak sources fall
below the floor. Score 0.85, the gate needs 1.0.
Gate not passed and rounds are left: search again.
The model rewrites the query in other words:
Round 2: the new words find a fourth, independent source: E4.
Only the new document is read: 0.62%.
Answer: 0.62%, from E3 and E4. It also says that the
second search round made the difference.
Question 2: what share of client crypto assets must be
kept in cold storage under the new authority rules?
Round 1: four documents found, but only the authority’s
Score 0.95: the gate needs two independent sources.
Not passed, rounds are left: search again.
Round 2: a new query, a new search, still no second source.
Round 3 ends the same way. The limit is three rounds.
Limit reached: no more searching. The run goes to a person.
The run pauses. Its state is saved as a checkpoint and can
wait for days, even across a restart.
The reviewer approves: the limited answer is published,
marked as reviewed. A rejection would withhold it.
Animation off (reduced motion). The model reads, the rules judge, a person decides.
